verdict: Plesk: Choose Plesk when hosting/server panel administration is the primary job on infrastructure you control. Scores use the IT & Development editorial methodology from first-party research as of 2026-08-18 — not hands-on product testing.
weaknesses: Per-server licence — different math from seat/agent tools
Edition matrix can confuse first-time buyers
bestFor: Web agencies and hosts administering sites on VPS/dedicated servers
Admins wanting GUI panel versus manual LAMP/stack configuration
Resellers needing Web Host multi-customer management
tradeoffs: Per-agent vs per-host vs per-seat vs per-GB pricing models
Module stacking and consumption overages vs single-SKU floors
Free tiers vs enterprise SSO/audit gates
Landscape-adjacent tools vs primary job-cluster peers on best pages
recommendation: Choose Plesk when hosting/server panel administration is the primary job on infrastructure you control. Compare Bright Data only on adjacent landscape pages for web-data jobs — not as a hosting-panel peer ranking.
editorialNotes: IT Wave-1 batch. Approved on it-development-editorial v1.0.0. membershipRole=primary. jobCluster=hosting-operations. handsOnTesting=false. Affiliate economics excluded.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Plesk targets web hosts and admins with GUI-first server management — approachable for hosting ops versus raw CLI-only administration.
Strong hosting-operations cluster fit — domains, mail, WordPress, and docker admin on owned servers.
Multi-site, reseller, and WordPress/docker tooling on Pro/Host editions give solid panel workflow depth for web ops.
WordPress/docker/Let’s Encrypt tooling is native; not a broad SaaS integration hub like ITSM or observability suites.
Panel RBAC and security extensions exist; enterprise SSO depth is limited versus cloud SaaS dev/IT platforms.
Web Host/reseller editions scale to multi-customer hosting businesses; licence tiers map to server growth.
~$16.99 Web Admin floor is competitive for VPS panel admin; higher editions and server counts raise TCO. Affiliate economics excluded.
No meaningful published ITSM/dev AI copilot — hosting panel job rarely needs AI scoring depth.

overallScoreRationale: Weighted average of the eight IT editorial criteria using category weights (IT job fit 16, workflow depth 14, ease of use 12, integrations 12, admin/security 12, value 12, AI 12, scalability 10), rounded to 1 decimal. Products are scored inside their job cluster — ITSM, observability, source control, hosting panels, and web-data platforms are not forced into one undifferentiated ranking. Not a hands-on lab score, and affiliate economics are excluded.
